extracted.intended_audience: general readers, social reformers, philanthropists, and policymakers
extracted.subtask_description: Descriptive, investigative reportage on tenement life, labor exploitation (sweaters), public health, and immigrant conditions in the urban East Side. Aimed at documenting social problems and informing reform discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factory labor law requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Ten hours is the legal work-day, and nine o'clock the closing hour at the latest. Forty-five minutes at least must be allowed for dinner, and children under sixteen must not be employed unless they can read and write English; none at all under fourteen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides the statutory baseline for acceptable factory labor conditions against which practice should be judged. The text cites these rules as the intended protections that are being undermined in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tenement workshop exemption / evasion of factory law
rubrics_metrics.description: The bulk of the sweater's work is done in the tenements, which the law that regulates factory labor does not reach. In the tenement the child works unchallenged from the day he is old enough to pull a thread; there is no such thing as a dinner hour; the 'day' is lengthened at both ends far into the night.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this criterion to identify illegal or exploitative labor practices: work carried out in private tenement rooms to evade factory regulation, extended hours, child labor, and home-based overtime by factory hands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public health / school hygiene instruction
rubrics_metrics.description: In the Allen Street public school the experienced principal has embodied among the elementary lessons a characteristic exercise asking daily: 'What must I do to be healthy?' and the school responds: 'I must keep my skin clean, Wear clean clothes, Breathe pure air, And live in the sunlight.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is presented as the official health curriculum; the author notes the gulf between instruction and reality, with teachers sometimes resorting to practical demonstration (wash-bowl and soap) to inculcate cleanliness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Municipal sanitary enforcement of food safety
rubrics_metrics.description: Health officers' cart precedes and follows policemen who shovel up with scant ceremony the eatables—musty bread, decayed fish and stale vegetables—indifferent to the curses that are showered on them from stoops and windows, and carry them off to the dump.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes the municipal standard/practice for removing unsafe food from markets; also notes the social friction this enforcement causes and implies questions about adequacy of enforcement tools (fines, raids).

rubrics_metrics.name: Philanthropic relief deployment principle: avoid pauperizing and perpetuating the problem
rubrics_metrics.description: To find proper channels through which to pour this money so that it shall effect its purpose without pauperizing, and without perpetuating the problem it is sought to solve, by attracting still greater swarms, is indeed no easy task.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guides donors and administrators to target relief so that it alleviates suffering without creating dependency or incentives that exacerbate immigration-driven overcrowding; the text discusses limitations of colonization and model-tenement approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teach immigrants the language first
rubrics_metrics.description: Its keynote evidently is the ignorance of the immigrants. They must be taught the language of the country they have chosen as their home, as the first and most necessary step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presents language instruction as the foundational reform: literacy and English competency are prerequisites for better employment prospects and for other educational or vocational programs to succeed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trade schools/manual training for the young are effective
rubrics_metrics.description: Trade schools for manual training could hardly be made to reach the adults, who in addition would have to be supported for months while learning. For the young this device has proved most excellent under the wise management of the United Hebrew Charities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocates vocational training targeted at youth as a practical, effective remedy; warns that adults are harder to retrain and require support during training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristics of the 'sweater' exploitative system
rubrics_metrics.description: The sweater is simply the middleman, the sub-contractor ... who drums up work among the clothing-houses. He drives his 'hands' as he drives his machine, for all they are worth, and makes a profit on their work ... The sweater knows well that the isolation of the workman in his helpless ignorance is his sure foundation, and he has done what he could ... to smother every symptom of awakening intelligence in his slaves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these markers to identify exploitative subcontracting: middleman control, use of immigrant labor pools, home-based (tenement) production to evade regulation, suppression of worker organization, very thin per-piece margins for labor and larger margins for contractors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relief strategy evaluation: limits of colonization and model tenements
rubrics_metrics.description: Colonization has not in the past been a success with these people. The great mass of them are too gregarious to take kindly to farming... To herd them in model tenements, though it relieve the physical suffering in a measure, would be to treat a symptom of the disease rather than strike at its root.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing interventions, prefer root-cause approaches (education, vocational training, language) over measures that only mitigate visible symptoms (model housing), and recognize cultural/social factors that limit certain programs' effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tenement overcrowding, lodging, and privacy standards (implicit)
rubrics_metrics.description: It has thousands upon thousands of lodgers who help to pay its extortionate rents. At night there is scarce a room in all the district that has not one or more of them, some above half a score, sleeping on cots, or on the floor. It is idle to speak of privacy in these 'homes.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use overcrowding, number of lodgers per room, sleeping arrangements (cots/floor), and lack of privacy as indicators of substandard housing that warrant intervention and regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanitation and public-safety hazards (fires, contaminated milk)
rubrics_metrics.description: Within a few years the police captured on the East Side a band of firebugs who made a business of setting fire to tenements for the insurance on their furniture... The sanitary authorities know what that means [cheap milk], know how miserably inadequate is the fine of fifty or a hundred dollars for the murder done in cold blood by the wretches who poison the babes of these tenements with the stuff that is half water, or swill.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies fire risk from arson/unsafe tenement practices and food/milk adulteration as urgent public-safety issues; notes that small fines are inadequate deterrents and that municipal regulation/enforcement must be strengthened.
